Secrets, database migrations, JAR files and third-party modules

What this lab adds: secrets, the database schema, modules and JARs

Part 1

Secrets

Database passwords and API keys configure the gateway, but can't be committed.

Part 2

Part 1: which values may never be committed, and where they live instead

02

Sort every value: public, per-environment or secret

Kind 1

Public

Port numbers, module lists, project names, timeouts, modules.json.

Committed, plain, in the repo
Kind 2

Per-environment

Gateway URLs, database names, container names. Same shape, different value per environment.

Committed defaults plus env vars or GitHub environment variables
Kind 3

Secret

Passwords, API keys, PATs, private keys, keystores. Anyone holding the value is you.

Never committed: .env, secret files, secret providers, GitHub secrets
03

A pushed secret stays in Git history: rotate it, don't just delete the line

# Monday, 09:14: "just to make it work"
git commit -m "wire up historian"
+ IGNITION_API_KEY = "ak_live_9f3ce81b..."
# Monday, 09:40: "phew, removed it"
git commit -m "oops, remove key"
- IGNITION_API_KEY = "ak_live_9f3ce81b..."
# anyone, any clone, any time later:
git log -p | grep ak_live
+ IGNITION_API_KEY = "ak_live_9f3ce81b..."  # still there
What to doRotate the credential, immediately: the old value is public now, so make it worthless. Scrubbing history afterwards is optional and never complete: every clone and fork keeps a copy.

Step through a leaked key, and why deleting the line fixes nothing. Monday 09:14: an API key is committed "just to make it work", and pushed. Monday 09:40: delete the line, commit, push. Fixed? No. The key sits in history, in every clone and fork: git log -p reads it right back. Rotate first. A pushed secret is a burned secret.

04

Four places a secret can live, and what each one leaks

0
Hardcoded in the repoplaintext in docker-compose.yaml or committed config
Leaks into: Git history, every clone, every fork. Never acceptable.
1
Env vars via .env and Compose interpolationwhat labs 02 to 05 already do
Out of Git. Still leaks into: docker inspect, compose config, the process env.
2
File-based secretsfiles mounted read-only at /run/secrets/<name>
Not in inspect, not in the process env. Each environment fills its own file.
2
Ignition 8.3 secret providersgateway config references a secret instead of containing it
The same config works on every gateway. Just as safe as a secret file. This lab uses both together.

Where a secret can live, from leaking most to leaking least. Hardcoded. In the repo, in history, in every fork. .env plus interpolation. Out of Git, still visible to docker inspect. File-based secrets. A file, not an env var, filled per environment. Secret providers. Just as safe: config stores a reference that a provider resolves from those files.

05

Move a password from an env var to a secret file, and out of docker inspect

Env var
# docker-compose.yaml
services:
  timescaledb:
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-lab06-postgres-pw}"

docker inspect lab06-timescaledb | grep PASSWORD
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD=lab06-postgres-pw
  # the value, in plaintext
Secret file
# docker-compose.yaml
secrets:
  postgres_password:
    file: ./secrets/postgres_password.txt   # gitignored
services:
  timescaledb:
    secrets: [postgres_password]
    environment:
      # the postgres image reads the _FILE suffix
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/postgres_password

docker inspect lab06-timescaledb | grep PASSWORD
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/postgres_password
  # only the path
06

Embedded vs referenced secrets in Ignition 8.3

Embedded secret

  • The gateway encrypts the value and stores the ciphertext in its own config.
  • It only decrypts on a gateway with the same encryption keys: on test it faults.
Fine for one gateway you manage by hand

Referenced secret

  • Config stores a reference: a provider name and a secret name, never the value.
  • A file-type secret provider resolves it from a file at /run/secrets/.
What a pipeline needs: no secret material in Git
07

One committed reference, and each gateway reads the value from its own file

TimescaleDB config.json, committed
"password": {
  "type": "Referenced",
  "data": {
    "providerName": "LabSecrets",
    "secretName": "POSTGRES_PASSWORD"
  }
}
a name, not a value
local/run/secrets/postgres_password is mounted from your secrets/postgres_password.txt
testthe same path, written by the deploy from the lab06-gateway-test secret
productionthe same path, written from the lab06-gateway-production secret
08

File-type secrets provider

  1. Provider LabSecretstype File: it holds paths, never values
  2. Secret POSTGRES_PASSWORDreads /run/secrets/postgres_password
  3. Connection passwordEmbedded becomes Referenced: provider plus secret name
secret-provider/LabSecrets/config.json
"profile":  { "type": "file" },
"settings": { "files": {
  "POSTGRES_PASSWORD": {
    "filePath": "/run/secrets/postgres_password",
    "fileType": "CLEARTEXT" } } }

Type Internal

You type the value into the gateway, which encrypts it under its own keys. Like an embedded secret, it only decrypts there.

09

Keep the provider in core and re-point the password in every deployment mode

  • The provider belongs in core. local-development never deploys: check where it landed with git status.
  • Every override has its own password. Re-point it in each mode. Create Override adds a mode to a connection.
What test resolves
externalthencorethentestneverlocal-development
# after every UI change: which collection did it land in?
git status

# where it must live, and where the passwords are
resources/core/ignition/secret-provider/LabSecrets/
resources/core/.../TimescaleDB/config.json        # Referenced
resources/test/.../TimescaleDB/config.json        # Referenced too:
resources/production/.../TimescaleDB/config.json  # each override
resources/local-development/.../TimescaleDB/...   # has its own field
10

The deploy workflow writes each environment's GitHub secrets to files in the gateway

  1. GitHub secreton the lab06-gateway-test or -production environment
  2. Materializea file in the workspace, umask 177 first
  3. Shipcopied to /run/secrets/ in the container
  4. Providerreads the file by name
  5. Referencein the committed config
  • Pass a secret through env: and write it with printf. Never put ${{ secrets.X }} in a run: line or an echo.
  • The files live in the container. A recreated container has none until the next deploy writes them again.
# lab06-deploy.yml (abridged)
environment: lab06-gateway-${{ inputs.target || 'test' }}
steps:
  - name: Materialize secret files
    env:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.POSTGRES_PASSWORD }}
    run: |
      umask 177                    # files land 0600
      mkdir -p secrets
      printf '%s' "$POSTGRES_PASSWORD" \
        > secrets/postgres_password.txt
  - name: Ship secret files into gateway container
    run: |
      docker cp secrets/postgres_password.txt \
        "$IGNITION_CONTAINER:/run/secrets/postgres_password"
11

What never goes into an Ignition repo, and the scan that checks it

  • .env, any real one. .env.example with placeholders is committed.
  • secrets/ contents: only the *.example files are tracked.
  • PATs and API keys: github_pat_..., ghp_..., runner registration tokens, gateway API keys.
  • Gateway backups (.gwbk) from real systems: users, DB connections and keystores in one file.
  • Keystores and TLS private keys: ssl.pfx, metro-keystore, *.p12.
# .gitignore: the relevant lines
.env
secrets/*
!secrets/*.example
*.gwbk

# the secret scan: tracked files under secrets/,
# known values in the payload
./scripts/validate.sh
# lab06-ci.yml runs the same scan on every PR
# stretch S3: gitleaks checks every commit of a PR

Part 2: version and deploy the database schema with your screens

12

Schema drift: a screen ships without the table it needs

What Git deploys to production
Perspective view "DowntimeLog"
  named query: SELECT reason, minutes
    FROM downtime_log ...
new screen, shipped
What the production database has
ignition_production=# \dt
  batch_log      present
  recipe_params  present
  downtime_log   missing
created by hand on test only, three weeks ago
  • "Worked on test", because someone created the table there by hand. Production was never told.
  • Schema changes become files in the repo, reviewed in the same PR as the screens that need them, applied by the pipeline.
13

db-init/ runs once, on an empty volume: it creates databases, it never changes them

# docker-compose.yaml: the timescaledb service
volumes:
  - ./db-init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro

# db-init/01-create-env-databases.sh (runs psql)
CREATE DATABASE ignition_test;
CREATE DATABASE ignition_production;
CREATE ROLE reporting LOGIN PASSWORD '...';
  • Day zero: the databases, the users and the extensions of a fresh environment.
  • Volume already exists? Nothing runs. Editing db-init/ after first boot changes nothing on test or production.
  • Every change after day zero is a migration.
14

Migrations: numbered SQL files, applied in order, tracked in the database

db-migration/migrate/
0001_create_production_kpi.up.sql + .down.sql
CREATE TABLE production_kpi (...);
INSERT INTO production_kpi ... ;  -- seed rows
0002_add_downtime_log.up.sql + .down.sql
CREATE TABLE downtime_log (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  reason TEXT, minutes INT, area TEXT);
0003_downtime_add_shift.up.sql + .down.sql
ALTER TABLE downtime_log
  ADD COLUMN shift TEXT;
migrate up
applies what's missing, in order
schema_migrations, inside each database
0001create production kpi: applied on test and production
0002add downtime log: applied on test and production
0003downtime add shift: pending on production, applies on the next deploy
The two rulesAlways pairs: up applies, down undoes. Never edit a migration after it deployed anywhere: fix mistakes with a new number.

We use golang-migrate. Build the ledger step by step. 0001, the first pair. The production_kpi table this lab ships with, as an up/down pair. 0002, a change. A new table, as a new pair. 0001 is never edited. 0003, another change. Each pair is numbered; order is the contract. migrate up compares the files with schema_migrations in the target database and applies only what's missing. Versioned, append-only, paired, tracked per database: Git for your schema.

15

The deploy migrates the database before the screens ship

  1. Secret fileswritten and shipped
  2. Modulesshipped, restart if changed
  3. Migrate DBmigrate up on the target environment's database
  4. Ship projects and configdocker cp into the gateway
  5. Scanprojects and config reload, no restart
  6. Smoke checkStatusPing answers

The migration fails: the run stops

No screen ships. The gateway keeps the old screens, which never needed the new table.

A screen ships before its table

The new screen queries a table that isn't there yet, and errors until the migration runs.

16

Rename a column without breaking a live screen: expand, switch, contract

Deploy 1

Expand

-- 0003_downtime_add_cause.up.sql
ALTER TABLE downtime_log
  ADD COLUMN cause TEXT;
UPDATE downtime_log
  SET cause = reason;   -- backfill

Old screens still read reason.

Deploy 2

Switch

-- the screens read the new column
SELECT cause, minutes, area
  FROM downtime_log ...

A normal screen PR: both columns exist.

Deploy 3

Contract

-- 0004_downtime_drop_reason.up.sql
ALTER TABLE downtime_log
  DROP COLUMN reason;

Once every environment runs the new screens.

One-step renameRENAME COLUMN in one migration breaks every screen that still selects reason, from the migrate step until the new screens ship.

Part 3: version and deploy third-party modules and JAR files instead of installing them by hand

17

Third-party modules: commit the .modl and load it from a folder

  1. Commit the binarythe .modl goes in third-party-modules/, tracked like any file
  2. Load from the folderevery gateway's command: points at it; modules load at boot
  3. Ship itthe deploy copies the modules and restarts the gateway when they changed
# docker-compose.yaml, every gateway's command: (already there)
-Dignition.gateway.externalModulesFolder=/third-party-modules
# /third-party-modules is where the repo folder is mounted in the container
18

Accept the license in config: the gateway writes the fingerprint and hash for you

  1. List the module id in all three compose env vars.
  2. Add a minimal entry to modules.json: only filename and onStartup.
  3. Boot once. The gateway accepts headlessly and writes certFingerprint and licenseAgreementHash into modules.json.
  4. Commit what it wrote. A fresh gateway now accepts from config alone.
# 1: compose env vars: the module id in all three
GATEWAY_MODULES_ENABLED:  ..., com.mussonindustrial.embr.charts
ACCEPT_MODULE_LICENSES:   ..., com.mussonindustrial.embr.charts
ACCEPT_MODULE_CERTS:      ..., com.mussonindustrial.embr.charts

# 2: modules.json: you write only these two lines
"com.mussonindustrial.embr.charts": {
  "filename": "/third-party-modules/Embr-Charts-Ignition83-4.0.1.modl",
  "onStartup": "enabled"
}

# 3: boot once: the gateway ADDS these itself
  "certFingerprint": "e5a3cf3f06627c175b68b0122ac8f2c3f9c992e2",
  "licenseAgreementHash": 3266212556
# 4: commit them
19

A module without its acceptance stops the gateway at commissioning: how to recover

Enabled, not accepted

StatusPing answers "details":"COMMISSIONING" until someone clicks accept. On a server nobody watches, the gateway is down.

Wiped volume, committed config

Commissioning creates a temp identity and rewrites security-properties. The scan API loses its permissions: 403.

# 1: acceptance back first, boot to RUNNING
git checkout -- docker-compose.yaml services/modules.json
docker compose up -d gateway-local-development
# 2: then undo what commissioning did, and restart
git checkout -- services/config/resources/core/ignition/security-properties/
rm -rf services/config/resources/core/ignition/{user-source,identity-provider}/temp
docker restart lab06-gateway-local-development
./scripts/scan.sh          # HTTP 200 again
20

JAR files: JDBC drivers ship inside the config tree, library JARs go on the classpath

Kind 1

JDBC drivers

An 8.3 config resource: the JAR sits next to its config.json in database-driver/PostgreSQL/ and ships with the config copy.

Kind 2

Library JARs

Java libraries your gateway scripts import. Pinned and committed, copied to lib/core/gateway/, loaded at boot.

  1. In the repojar-files/jar/commons-csv-1.14.1.jar
  2. On the classpathcopied to lib/core/gateway/
  3. Restartlibrary JARs load at boot, like modules
  4. Import itin any gateway-scoped script: from org.apache.commons.csv import CSVFormat
21

A Perspective property binding with a script transform, in the shape the CI linter accepts

  • Property binding: a component property follows a path such as view.custom.line. Bidirectional lets an input write back into it.
  • Script transform: Jython that runs on the gateway, gets the bound value and returns what the property shows. Imports go inside it.
  • No sibling paths: ign-lint rejects ../TextField.props.text. Share state through a view custom property.
  • Warnings fail the lint job too: keep custom property names plain, line, not csvLine.
# view.json, abridged: the label's binding
"custom": { "line": "" },
...
"meta": { "name": "Label" },
"propConfig": { "props.text": { "binding": {
  "type": "property",
  "config": { "path": "view.custom.line" },
  "transforms": [{ "type": "script", "code":
    from org.apache.commons.csv import CSVFormat
    from java.io import StringReader
    records = CSVFormat.DEFAULT.parse(
        StringReader(value or "")).getRecords()
    return " | ".join(records[0]) if records else ""
  }] } } }
